item.title: Water Cycle With Exact Labels

turns.text: Make a 10-second widescreen water-cycle explainer with a friendly voice-over you write. Show water rising, clouds forming, then rain. Label those stages exactly “Evaporation”, “Condensation”, and “Precipitation”, in that order. No other on-screen text.

item.tests: Tests exact rendered labels, correct stage mapping, and coordinated original narration in a short explainer.

answer_sheet.Exact on-screen labels: Evaporation; Condensation; Precipitation. Use that capitalization and order, without quotation marks.
answer_sheet.Other text: No other on-screen text, including subtitles.
answer_sheet.Voice and language: Friendly English voice; specific voice is your call.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second widescreen video has a friendly, intelligible English voice-over explaining the depicted cycle.
Water rises as vapor, clouds form, and rain falls, in that order.
The visible labels read exactly 'Evaporation', 'Condensation', and 'Precipitation', with no misspellings.
Each label is legible and appears with its corresponding stage, in the requested order.

turns.text: Could you make a water-cycle explainer with a friendly voice-over that you write? I always find this process easier to understand when I can actually watch it happen. What I mean is, show water rising, then clouds forming, then rain, and make it 10 seconds long in widescreen. For those stages, use the exact labels “Evaporation”, “Condensation”, and “Precipitation”, in that order. I’m probably over-explaining because I worry about getting the stages mixed up. Please don’t put any other text on screen.
turns.agent:
I couldn’t generate the video because your Magic Hour account has insufficient credits. No video was created.

The prepared 10-second widescreen sequence is:
- **0–3 seconds:** Water vapor rises — “Evaporation”
- **3–6 seconds:** Clouds form — “Condensation”
- **6–10 seconds:** Rain falls — “Precipitation”

**Friendly voice-over:** “Sun warms water, and it rises as vapor. It cools, forming clouds. Then rain falls back down.”

No other on-screen text is planned.
